metadata.description: Parameterised code-generation templates for the Programming Language Tutor Chatbot. Used by the generate_code intent. Each template fills {{placeholder}} values with safe, validated parameters and returns the filled code plus an explanation. No user code is executed.

templates.title: Hello World / Print Output
templates.template: print('{{message}}')
templates.filled_example: print('Hello, World!')
templates.explanation: print() displays text to the console. The text inside the quotes is called a string literal. Every time this program runs it shows the message.
templates.notes: Safe to generate. Single print statement.

templates.title: Variables and Basic Types
templates.template:
{{int_var}} = {{int_val}}
{{float_var}} = {{float_val}}
{{str_var}} = '{{str_val}}'

print(f'{{int_var}} = {{{{{int_var}}}}')
print(f'{{float_var}} = {{{{{float_var}}}}')
print(f'{{str_var}} = {{{{{str_var}}}}')
print(type({{int_var}}))
templates.filled_example:
age = 20
gpa = 3.9
name = 'Alice'

print(f'age = {age}')
print(f'gpa = {gpa}')
print(f'name = {name}')
print(type(age))
templates.explanation: Python does not require type declarations. The variable name is written on the left, the value on the right. type() shows the data type. int is a whole number, float is decimal, str is text.
templates.notes: Safe to generate. No input required.

templates.title: Read User Input and Display Output

parameters.name: prompt
parameters.description: The prompt shown to the user

templates.template:
{{var_name}} = input('{{prompt}}: ')
print(f'{{greeting}}, {{{{{var_name}}}}}!')
templates.filled_example:
name = input('Enter your name: ')
print(f'Hello, {name}!')
templates.explanation: input() reads a line of text from the keyboard and returns it as a string. The f-string uses curly braces {} to embed the variable value directly into the output.
templates.notes: Safe to generate. Uses input().

templates.title: Addition of Two Numbers
templates.template:
{{var1}} = float(input('Enter first number: '))
{{var2}} = float(input('Enter second number: '))
{{result_var}} = {{var1}} + {{var2}}
print(f'{{{{{var1}}}}} + {{{{{var2}}}}} = {{{{{result_var}}}}}')
templates.filled_example:
a = float(input('Enter first number: '))
b = float(input('Enter second number: '))

print(f'{a} + {b} = {result}')
templates.explanation: float(input(...)) reads a number from the keyboard â€” input() returns a string so float() converts it to a decimal number. The + operator adds them. The f-string displays all three values.
templates.notes: Safe to generate. Uses input() and float conversion.

templates.title: Simple Calculator (add, subtract, multiply, divide)
templates.explanation: The program reads two numbers and an operator from the user. An if-elif chain checks which operator was entered and performs the matching calculation. Division includes a guard against dividing by zero.
templates.notes: Safe to generate. Includes zero-division guard.

templates.title: If-Else Decision
templates.explanation: The if statement checks the condition. If it is True the first block runs; otherwise the else block runs. Python uses indentation (4 spaces) to show which lines belong to each block.
templates.notes: Safe to generate. Simple two-branch decision.

templates.title: Grade Calculator
templates.template:
name = input('Enter student name: ')
num_subjects = int(input('How many subjects? '))

total = 0
for i in range(1, num_subjects + 1):
    score = float(input(f'Enter score for Subject {i}: '))
    total += score

average = total / num_subjects

if average >= 90:
    grade = 'A'
elif average >= 80:
    grade = 'B'
elif average >= 70:
    grade = 'C'
elif average >= 60:
    grade = 'D'
else:
    grade = 'F'

print(f'\n--- Student Grade Report ---')
print(f'Student Name : {name}')
print(f'Average Score: {average:.2f}')
print(f'Final Grade  : {grade}')

templates.title: For Loop with range()
templates.template:
for {{var}} in range({{start}}, {{end}}):
    print({{var}})
templates.filled_example:
for i in range(1, 6):
    print(i)
templates.explanation: range(1, 6) generates the sequence 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 â€” the second number is excluded. The for loop assigns each value to i in turn and runs the indented block.
templates.notes: Safe to generate. Basic counting loop.

templates.title: While Loop with Counter
templates.template:
{{var}} = 1
while {{var}} <= {{limit}}:
    print({{var}})
    {{var}} += 1
templates.filled_example:
count = 1
while count <= 5:
    print(count)
    count += 1
templates.explanation: The while loop keeps running as long as count <= 5. count starts at 1 and increases by 1 each iteration. Forgetting count += 1 would create an infinite loop.
templates.notes: Safe to generate. Counter-controlled while loop.

templates.title: Nested Loop â€” Multiplication Table
templates.explanation: The outer loop controls the row (i) and the inner loop controls the column (j). For each row, every column is printed on the same line using end=''. print() with no arguments moves to the next line after each row. :4 right-aligns each number in a 4-character field.
templates.notes: Safe to generate. O(n^2) nested loop â€” keep n small.

templates.title: Function Definition and Call
templates.filled_example:

    return f'Hello, {name}!'

# Call the function

print(result)
templates.explanation: def defines a function. The parameter name receives the value passed in the function call. return sends the result back to the caller. The function is then called with 'Alice' as the argument.
templates.notes: Safe to generate. Single-parameter function.

for item in {{list_name}}:
    print(item)

print(f'Total items: {len({{list_name}})}')
print(f'Sum: {sum({{list_name}})}')
print(f'Average: {sum({{list_name}}) / len({{list_name}}):.2f}')

templates.explanation: The list is created with square brackets and comma-separated values. The for loop iterates over each item. len() returns the count, sum() adds all values. :.2f formats the average to 2 decimal places.
templates.notes: Safe to generate. Read-only list iteration.

templates.title: String Operations

print(f'Lowercase: {{{{{var}}}}}.lower()}')

print(math.pow(2, 8))     # 256.0
print(math.floor(3.9))    # 3

templates.title: Grocery Calculator
templates.template:
total = 0.0
print('Grocery Calculator (type {{stop_word}} to finish)')
while True:
    item = input('Item name: ').strip()
    if item.lower() == '{{stop_word}}':
        break
    price    = float(input(f'Price of {item}: '))
    qty      = int(input(f'Quantity of {item}: '))
    subtotal = price * qty
    total   += subtotal
    print(f'  Subtotal: {subtotal:.2f}')
print(f'\nTotal bill: {total:.2f}')

templates.template:
def print_board(b):
    for row in b:
        print(' | '.join(row))
        print('-' * 9)

def check_winner(b, mark):
    for i in range(3):
        if all(b[i][j]==mark for j in range(3)): return True
        if all(b[j][i]==mark for j in range(3)): return True
    return b[0][0]==b[1][1]==b[2][2]==mark or b[0][2]==b[1][1]==b[2][0]==mark

board   = [[str(i*3+j+1) for j in range(3)] for i in range(3)]
current = 'X'
for _ in range(9):
    print_board(board)
    move = int(input(f'Player {current} (1-9): '))
    row, col = (move-1)//3, (move-1)%3
    board[row][col] = current
    if check_winner(board, current):
        print_board(board)
        print(f'Player {current} wins!')
        break
    current = 'O' if current=='X' else 'X'
else:
    print_board(board)
    print('Draw!')

templates.title: Text File Analyzer

parameters.name: sample_text
parameters.default: The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog

templates.template:
TEXT='{{sample_text}}'
lines=TEXT.strip().split('\n')
words=TEXT.lower().split()
chars=len(TEXT.replace(' ','').replace('\n',''))
punct=set('.,!?;:\'"')
clean=[w.strip(''.join(punct)) for w in words]
freq={}
for w in clean:
    if w:freq[w]=freq.get(w,0)+1
top5=sorted(freq.items(),key=lambda x:-x[1])[:5]
print('=== Text Analysis ===')
print(f'Lines     : {len(lines)}')
print(f'Words     : {len(words)}')
print(f'Characters: {chars}')
print(f'Unique    : {len(freq)}')
print('\nTop 5 words:')
for word,count in top5:print(f'  {word:<15} {count}')
templates.explanation: Hardcoded string analyzed in-memory. sorted with lambda sorts by count descending.

templates.title: Python Dictionary
templates.template:
student = {
    '{{key1}}': '{{val1}}',
    '{{key2}}': {{val2}},
    'enrolled': True
}

# Access
print(student['{{key1}}'])

# Add / update
student['gpa'] = 3.9

# Check key
if '{{key2}}' in student:
    print(f'{{{{key2}}}}: {{student["{{key2}}"]}}')

# Iterate
for key, value in student.items():
    print(f'{{key}}: {{value}}')
templates.explanation: Dictionaries store key-value pairs. Keys must be unique and immutable. .items() iterates both. in checks key existence. dict.get(key, default) avoids KeyError.

templates.title: Python Set
templates.template:
a = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5}
b = {4, 5, 6, 7, 8}

print('Union:',       a | b)
print('Intersection:', a & b)
print('Difference:',   a - b)
print('Symmetric diff:', a ^ b)

# Sets remove duplicates automatically
nums = [1, 2, 2, 3, 3, 3]
unique = set(nums)
print('Unique:', unique)

# Membership test (O(1))
print(3 in a)

templates.explanation: Sets store unique unordered values. | is union, & is intersection, - is difference. In-test is O(1) â€” much faster than lists for membership checks.

templates.title: Python Tuple
templates.template:
# Create a tuple
coords = (10.5, 20.3)
rgb    = (255, 128, 0)

# Access
print(coords[0])
print(rgb[-1])

# Unpack
x, y = coords
print(f'x={x}, y={y}')

# Tuples are immutable â€” this would raise TypeError:
# coords[0] = 99

# Named tuple
from collections import namedtuple
Point = namedtuple('Point', ['x', 'y'])
p = Point(3, 4)
print(f'Point: x={p.x}, y={p.y}')
print(f'Distance: {(p.x**2 + p.y**2)**0.5:.2f}')

templates.title: Java Methods
templates.explanation: Java methods need a return type, name, and parameter list. void returns nothing. static belongs to the class, not an object. Instance methods need an object to call them.

templates.title: Java Inheritance
templates.explanation: extends creates a subclass. super() calls the parent constructor. @Override marks a method that replaces the parent's version. The child inherits all public/protected methods of the parent.

templates.title: Java Interface
templates.explanation: Interfaces define a contract â€” any class that implements it must provide those methods. default methods have a body and are optional to override. A class can implement multiple interfaces.

templates.title: Java ArrayList and HashMap
templates.filled_example:
import java.util.*;
public class CollectionsDemo { public static void main(String[] args) { ArrayList<String> names=new ArrayList<>(); names.add("Alice"); names.add("Bob"); names.add("Charlie"); System.out.println(names); Collections.sort(names); System.out.println(names); HashMap<String,Integer> scores=new HashMap<>(); scores.put("Alice",95); scores.put("Bob",88); System.out.println(scores.get("Alice")); for(Map.Entry<String,Integer> e:scores.entrySet()) System.out.println(e.getKey()+": "+e.getValue()); } }
templates.explanation: ArrayList is a resizable array â€” add(), get(), remove(), sort(). HashMap stores key-value pairs â€” put(), get(), containsKey(). entrySet() iterates all pairs. Both are generic â€” <String, Integer> specifies the types.

templates.title: C Pointers
templates.explanation: & gets the address of a variable. * in a declaration means pointer type. * in an expression dereferences (reads/writes the value). Pointer arithmetic moves by element size â€” p+1 points to the next int.

templates.title: C Structures (struct)
templates.explanation: typedef struct creates a reusable type. Members are accessed with the dot operator. strncpy is safer than strcpy â€” it limits the number of characters copied. Arrays of structs hold multiple records.

templates.title: C Dynamic Memory (malloc / free)
templates.explanation: malloc allocates bytes on the heap and returns a pointer. Always check if NULL (allocation failed). sizeof(int) makes the size portable. free() releases the memory. Setting to NULL after free prevents use-after-free bugs. calloc zeroes memory.

templates.title: Java Method (Function)
templates.explanation: Java methods need a return type, a name, and parameters. static means you call it on the class, not an instance. void means no return value.

templates.title: Java Import and Standard Library
templates.explanation: Java uses import to bring in classes from packages. java.lang is automatic. Math, Collections, ArrayList are from java.util and java.lang.

templates.title: C #include and Standard Library
templates.explanation: #include copies a header file into your source. stdio.h for I/O, math.h for math, string.h for strings, stdlib.h for memory/random, time.h for time. Link with -lm for math.h.

templates.title: Python def â€” Define a Function
templates.template:
def {{func_name}}({{param}}='{{default}}'):
    """Greets a person by name."""
    return f'Hello, {{{{{param}}}}}!'

# Function with default argument
def power(base, exp=2):
    return base ** exp

print({{func_name}}())
print({{func_name}}('Alice'))
print(add(3, 4))
print(power(3))
print(power(2, 8))
